c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: What is the difference between `else if` and a second, separate `if`?

B.text: `else if` is only asked when the test before it was false

c1.why: An `else if` sits in the same chain. Once one branch has run, the rest are skipped — separate `if` blocks are all asked, every time.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: Why does this car need two thresholds instead of one?

A.text: One line gives near and far but no place to hold still

C.text: To use up the `else if` block

c2.why: A single split point means the car is always either advancing or retreating. The gap between two numbers is where "just right" lives.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: What happens if you make the hold band very narrow — say between 9 and 10cm?

C.text: The car twitches back and forth constantly

c3.why: Real readings wobble. A band too narrow to contain that wobble sends the car in and out of it non-stop.

r1.label: Q1
r1.prompt: Your hand is 3cm from the sensor. What does the car do?
r1.why: 3 is below 5, so the first branch runs and both wheels reverse.

r2.label: Q2
r2.prompt: Your hand is 7cm away. What does the car do?
r2.why: 7 fails the first test but passes the second, so the middle branch runs — and `0, 0` is "stay where you are".

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: You move your hand slowly away from the car. What does it do?
r3.why: Once the gap passes 10 the last branch takes over and drives forward — which closes the gap again.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: These are two separate `if` blocks. Your hand is 3cm away — what actually reaches the motors?
r4.why: 3 passes both tests, so both branches run — and the second one overwrites the first. The car stops instead of backing away.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: This car drives into your hand instead of holding a gap. What is wrong?

A.text: The tests are in the wrong order — `< 10` catches everything first

C.text: The reading is outside the loop

d1.why: In a chain the first true test wins. `< 10` is true whenever `< 5` is, so the reverse branch can never be reached — and that first branch holds the forward block, so anything inside 10 cm drives in. Fixing it takes both: `< 5` first, and stop (not forward) in the `< 10` branch.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: This car never holds still — it is always moving in or out. What is missing?

A.text: The middle branch that stops the wheels

d2.why: With only two branches there is no gap between them. The band where the car rests has to be a branch of its own.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: The tests use `<`, like our program (`< 5`, `< 10`). Put the three branches in the order they must be tested: 1 too far — come forward · 2 too close — back away · 3 just right — hold still
b1.why: In an `else if` chain the tightest test comes first. Then the middle band, and everything else falls through to the last branch.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: The `else if` branch holds still. You want the car to hold between 8cm and 15cm. Which pair of tests does that?
b2.why: Smallest first. The second test then means "not below 8, but below 15" — which is exactly the band.
